Indicator: Number of SAPS-owned firearms confirmed as lost
Outcome: Priority 6: Social Cohesion and Safer Communities

ReasonforDeviation_Q1: The Department has implemented several measures to reduce firearm losses, including providing members with safes and retention cords. Despite these efforts, the rise in robberies in townships and other areas, as well as incidents of housebreaking, vehicle theft, and personal theft, contribute to ongoing losses. Given the nature of police work, the risk of firearm loss is ever-present. It is the responsibility of each member to safeguard their issued firearm, following the preventive measures established by the department. Preventing firearm losses remains a top priority for the Department.
CorrectiveAction_Q1:
Every
loss is thoroughly investigated regardless of the circumstances.
ReasonforDeviation_Q2: The escalation of robbery in township or other place, as well as housebreaking (property locked), negligence of members, theft from a dwelling and loss from person.
CorrectiveAction_Q2: In order to prevent the loss of SAPS-owned firearms, the following measures are implemented: the barcoding and marking of all SAPS-owned firearms with the SAPS emblem, IBIS testing to generate firearm profiles, biannual inspections, the issuance of safes to members for the safekeeping of firearms, the issuance of retention cords, daily parade inspections, control over and the safekeeping of firearms not under the direct and physical control of a member and inspections by Designated Supply Chain Management Armourers. Additionally, provincial corrective measures will involve the implementation and enforcement of the provincial directive on the safe custody of state firearms, the establishment of a Firearm Risk Committee at business units, the enhancement of the Firearm Management Plan and the conducting of unannounced firearm inspections by District Commissioners.
ReasonforDeviation_Q3: The increase in incidents of robbery, whether in townships or other places, as well as housebreaking (property locked), loss from person, as well as theft from offices or store.
CorrectiveAction_Q3: Measures taken to prevent the loss of SAPS-owned firearms, include the bar coding and the marking of all SAPS-owned firearms with the SAPS emblem, IBIS testing to create firearm profiles, biannual inspections, the issuing of safes to members for the safekeeping of firearms, the issuing of retention cords, daily parade inspections, control over and the safekeeping of firearms not under the direct and physical control of a member and inspections by Designated Supply Chain Management Armorers. Furthermore, the Firearm tracking solution was evaluated by Technology Management Service (TMS).
ReasonforDeviation_Q4:
The implementation of the revised Loss Management 
Process, as outlined in National Instruction 6 of 2024 on the Management of Losses in the SAPS, along with the updated Standard Operating Procedure for Balance Adjustments on the Provisioning Administration System, contributed significantly to the overachievement. These measures enhanced the management of losses and improved overall data integrity. A noticeable decline was also recorded in serious crimes against SAPS members, including robberies in townships and other areas, housebreaking, property losses and theft from private vehicles. Furthermore, provinces and divisions conducted regular inspections and awareness drives to educate members on the safe storage of firearms. Quarterly communication was maintained through letters sent to all provinces and divisions, aimed at streamlining processes, enhancing information integrity and strengthening system controls, all of which contributed positively to the reduction in losses.

Addressing these underlying causes of crime requires long-term economic, social and developmental interventions that extend beyond the scope of immediate police responses.  initiated Operation Shanela, in May 2023, which is supported by the Enhanced Crime Prevention and Combating Action Plan (ICPCAP). The Operation provides for coordinated weekly mandatory (simultaneous and high density) integrated and multidiscipllinary operations in priority police station areas. The Operation, which has now been renamed High Density since 1 June 2024 also provide for an increased community mobilisation against crime in collaboration with Community Police Forums and other relevant concerned partners, focusing on the top 30 national and top 10 provincial police stations contributing to the highest reported incidence of contact crime and Gender-Based Violence (GBV). CorrectiveAction_Q4: The National Policing Strategy mandates that provinces failing to meet their targets must revisit their crime analysis and plans, developing comprehensive strategies based on this analysis. Police intervention should be driven by the analysis and not limited to specific days of the week. Districts and provinces must support prioritised police stations accordingly. If stabilisation is needed beyond provincial capacity, submissions should be made to the DNC Policing for consideration of national intervention.

ReasonforDeviation_Q2:

Acquisition of a water reserve system.

ReasonforDeviation_Q3:
Water supply disruptions at the Biology Laboratory, in Arcadia.
The turnaround time has been impacted by an increase in the number of cases received.
Accommodation and environmental conditions are compromised due to the malfunctioning of building equipment, such as extractors and air conditioning systems, which adversely affects instrumentation and ventilation. The KZN laboratory has not been utilised to its full potential since the occurrence of the flooding.
The efficiency of the LIMS is consistently slow or non-functional.
CorrectiveAction_Q3:
Acquisition of a water backup system.  
Focussing on the provisioning of reports for court-driven cases. Prioritising the finalisation of the oldest, balanced with the finalisation of new cases before they exceed their specified timelines.
Continuous communication between the SCM Division and the DPWI. 
The needs assessments, along with the USAS document, have been forwarded to the SMC Division for further processing in collaboration with the DPWI concerning both permanent accommodation in Pinetown and alternative accommodation options. 
Ongoing communication with the TMS Division regarding system performance.
System challenges takes too long to be addressed by TMS.
ReasonforDeviation_Q4: Since the flooding in 2016, KZN lacks a fully functional laboratory. As a result, drug analysis cases are received and registered in Pretoria, then transported to the Western Cape for processing by KZN personnel. Additionally, due to the absence of DNA processing capabilities in KZN (except for Evidence Recovery), DNA cases are sent to Pretoria for analysis. Maintenance and repairs to the building infrastructure (e.g., taps, water pipes, air conditioners, toilets) are delayed due to lengthy approval processes, which hinders optimal instrument functionality and causes delays in case processing. While the decentralisation of services in Mpumalanga is expected to improve space constraints, its implementation has been slow, despite its prior approval. The Biology Laboratory at Arcadia was closed due to flooding, exacerbating the existing infrastructure issues. The influx of complex cases has resulted in longer turnaround times. The turnaround time has been affected by the high volume of cases being received. The introduction of the LIMS has impeded the Chemistry Section's ability to finalise entries promptly. The laboratory is under-capacitated due to personnel losses. Although new staff have been appointed, it takes nearly two years for analysts to become fully trained and work independently.
CorrectiveAction_Q4: Efforts are underway to source alternative accommodation in Durban Central and permanent facilities in Pinetown, with an approach being made to acquire a suitable building as a turnkey project while closely monitoring the effectiveness of plans for the construction of a new facility. Continuous communication between the FSL, SCM and the DPW&I to prioritise the procurement of maintenance contracts for FSL Western Cape, FSL Biology, FSL Silverton, FSL KwaZulu-Natal and other affected laboratories to ensure sustained operations. Ensuring the effective implementation of the six-month interim maintenance plan while the long-term contract is being finalised. Strategic engagements with the SCM Division and the DPW&I and needs assessments for Mpumalanga were submitted to the DPW&I (currently awaiting a feasibility study between the DPW&I and the SCM Division) and engagement to secure approvals for the SAPS to execute urgent maintenance. The focus on delivering reports for court-driven cases, addressing the oldest cases, while finalising new cases before their timelines are exceeded. Additionally, continuous collaboration with TMS and SITA aims to resolve any operational gaps affecting the output and the ongoing appointment and training of new analysts to increasing capacity and developing long-term retention strategies.
